transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I've been struggling with some really intense beliefs and hearing voices that others can't hear, which has been happening off and on for over two years now. During these times, I also get extremely energetic and my thoughts just race out of control. It has been really hard to deal with.

Have there been times when you heard voices or had unusual beliefs for at least two weeks even when you were not feeling unusually energetic or having racing thoughts? Or do those experiences only happen during those high-energy periods?

Yes, there have definitely been times lasting at least two weeks where I still heard those voices and had those strong beliefs, even when my mood and energy levels were completely normal. They don't just happen during those high-energy periods; they can happen when I'm feeling totally ordinary, too.
Over the whole time you’ve been ill, have those high-energy or manic periods been present for most of the illness, or have they happened only during a smaller portion of the time?
Yes, those high-energy periods have definitely been present for most of the time since I first got sick. They've made up the majority of my illness, rather than just being a small part of it.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were ["Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)", "Schizophrenia"]. Based on this conversation, Schizophrenia seems unlikely because the patient reports clear manic/high-energy periods that have been present for most of the total duration of the illness, and there have also been at least two weeks of psychotic symptoms occurring when mood was normal. This pattern fits Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type) rather than Schizophrenia. Therefore the current candidate list is narrowed to ["Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)"].

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a history of psychotic symptoms (voices and intense beliefs) for over two years, with at least a two-week period of psychosis occurring in the absence of mood symptoms, which supports a primary psychotic process. They also report recurrent high-energy periods with racing thoughts consistent with mania, and these mood episodes have been present for the majority of the total illness duration, supporting schizoaffective disorder bipolar type rather than schizophrenia or bipolar disorder with psychotic features.
